en.title: Baby Sleep: Safe Sleep and Calmer Nights (Up to One Year)
en.description: Four lessons for parents from birth until the first birthday: prepare a safe space for every sleep, understand waking and night feeds, read tired and sleepy cues, and keep a short, calm bedtime routine; throughout, tell normal variation apart from danger signs needing urgent help.

paths.band_notes: Birth until first birthday only; prenatal-1 is the canonical band. This recovery publishes only the first four contiguous lessons; the remaining six original drafts stay held in the preserved backup. Lessons 3-4 follow CDC milestone tips (2, 4 and 9 months), AAP drowsy-but-awake from about 4 months, and NHS bedtime-routine guidance; no routine length, no deadline, and no unit outside prenatal-1. Follow AAP safe sleep and NHS infant feeding/waking guidance. Never delay responding to hunger or distress, never recommend leaving a newborn to cry, never promise a sleep-training deadline. Inability to wake, stopped breathing, or blue/grey colour requires emergency help immediately.

lessons.title: النوم الآمن: على ظهره في سريرٍ خالٍ
lessons.focus: Safe sleep for every sleep: on the back, a firm flat surface, nothing soft in the cot, own sleep surface in the parents' room, never on a sofa or armchair with a parent, no overheating, a smoke-free home; supervised tummy time while awake.

lessons.title: كم ينام الرضيع؟ ولماذا يستيقظ كثيرًا؟
lessons.focus: Normal infant sleep: many hours in short stretches, frequent waking to feed in the first months, gradual lengthening of night sleep, wide differences between babies; what is normal versus worrying.

lessons.title: علامات النعاس: اللحظة المناسبة للنوم
lessons.focus: Reading tired signals (turning the head away, yawning, fussing — CDC), responding without fear of spoiling, winding down, placing the sleepy baby on the back in a safe sleep space, moving a baby who fell asleep in a car seat/swing/carrier to a firm flat surface; dozing at feeds is normal early on; from about 4 months put down drowsy (AAP); ordinary sleepiness versus emergency signs (NHS).

lessons.title: روتينٌ قصير قبل النوم
lessons.focus: A simple, soothing bedtime routine (NHS): bath or wash, fresh nappy and night clothes, dim lights, a lullaby or quiet du'a, a cuddle, then the cot; routines help the baby learn what to expect (CDC); calm night feeds; always ending in safe sleep; no promised result or fixed length; adjust as the baby grows.

en.title: Toddler Sleep: A Steady Routine and Calmer Nights (Ages 2-3)
en.description: A daily path for parents of two- and three-year-olds: how much sleep they need, a steady evening routine, moving to their own bed, night waking, naps, routines upset by illness and travel, night-time fears, resisting bedtime, and when to see the doctor.

paths.band_notes: Ages 2-3: need about 11-14 hours of sleep in 24 hours including the nap; love routine; separation and night fears are common; resistance to bedtime is normal testing. Conservative medical advice; snoring and breathing pauses need a doctor.

lessons.title: كم يحتاج طفلك من النوم؟
lessons.focus: Sleep needs at two and three including the nap, signs that a child is not sleeping enough (irritability, frequent tantrums, falling asleep in the car), and setting the bedtime by counting back from the wake time.

lessons.title: روتين المساء: الخطوات نفسها كل ليلة
lessons.focus: A short evening routine in the same order every night (bath, pyjamas, story, dim light), no longer than about twenty minutes, so the predictability itself calms the child.

lessons.title: ضعه في سريره نعسانًا لا نائمًا
lessons.focus: Why the last moment before sleep should be in their own bed rather than in arms; the sleep association that makes them call for you at night; how to start.

lessons.title: من سريرك إلى سريره: خطةٌ تدريجية
lessons.focus: A gradual plan to move the child to their own bed: sitting beside them with a hand on them, then without touching, then on a chair, moving closer to the door every few nights; expect setbacks.

lessons.title: الاستيقاظ ليلًا: طمأنةٌ قصيرة بلا لعب
lessons.focus: Responding to night waking: a brief reassurance in their own bed, low light, few words, no picking up or play, the same response every time.

lessons.title: القيلولة: متى تبقى ومتى تقصر
lessons.focus: Most two-year-olds still need one daytime nap; a late or very long nap pushes bedtime; signs a child is ready to drop the nap; quiet time instead.

lessons.title: حين يتعطّل الروتين: مرضٌ أو سفرٌ أو أخٌ جديد
lessons.focus: Sleep setbacks after illness, travel, a move or a new baby are expected; meet the extra need calmly, then return to the routine from the previous step without frustration.

lessons.title: مخاوف الليل والأحلام المزعجة
lessons.focus: Fear of the dark and separation at night are normal at this age: a dim night light, a short goodbye routine, reassurance without mocking; frightening dreams versus night terrors (stay calm, keep the child safe, don't wake them); when to ask the doctor.

lessons.title: «لا أريد أن أنام»: مقاومة موعد النوم
lessons.focus: Bedtime resistance: a fixed time, no question whose answer can be no, two small choices within the routine, a calm firm return to bed, no long negotiation.

lessons.title: متى تستشير الطبيب في نوم طفلك؟
lessons.focus: Signs that need a doctor: loud snoring most nights, pauses in breathing, breathing through the mouth, very restless sleep, sleepiness or behaviour problems in the day, frequent night terrors, sleepwalking with danger, a sudden change in sleep.

create.title: النوم في سنّ ما قبل المدرسة: مواعيد ثابتة وليالٍ هادئة (4-6 سنوات)
create.description: مسار يومي للوالدين مع طفلٍ بين الرابعة والسادسة: ساعات النوم التي يحتاجها، والموعد الثابت، ونصف الساعة الهادئة قبل النوم، والخوف من الظلام، والمجيء إلى سرير الوالدين ليلًا، والشاشات، والحركة في النهار، والتبوّل الليلي، وأذكار النوم، ومتى تستشير الطبيب.

en.title: Sleep in the Preschool Years: Steady Times and Calm Nights (Ages 4-6)
en.description: A daily path for parents of four- to six-year-olds: the hours of sleep they need, a fixed bedtime, a calm half hour before sleep, fear of the dark, coming to the parents' bed at night, screens, daytime activity, bedwetting, bedtime adhkar, and when to see the doctor.

paths.band_notes: Ages 4-6: need about 10-13 hours of sleep including any nap; vivid imagination makes fears of the dark common; bedwetting is still common and never a reason for punishment. Conservative medical advice.

lessons.title: كم ساعةً يحتاج طفلك من النوم؟
lessons.focus: Sleep needs at four to six, the link between sleep and mood, attention and growth, and counting back from the wake-up time to set bedtime.

lessons.title: موعدٌ واحد طوال الأسبوع
lessons.focus: One bedtime and one wake-up time every day of the week, including weekends and holidays, and why a steady body clock makes falling asleep easier.

lessons.title: نصف ساعةٍ هادئة قبل النوم
lessons.focus: A calm half hour before bed: no screens, no rough play, no heavy food; a bath, a story, a talk about the day, dim lights.

lessons.title: الخوف من الظلام
lessons.focus: Fear of the dark and of monsters is a normal part of imagination: acknowledge it, don't mock or force, a dim night light or favourite toy, no frightening stories before bed, small brave steps.

lessons.title: حين يأتي إلى سريرك ليلًا
lessons.focus: When the child comes to the parents' bed at night: walk them back calmly and firmly, few words, the same response every time, praise mornings in their own bed.

lessons.title: الشاشات والنوم
lessons.focus: Screens before bed delay sleep and stir the mind; screens out of the bedroom, switched off an hour before bed; replacing them with a story or quiet play.

lessons.title: حركةٌ في النهار، نومٌ في الليل
lessons.focus: Active outdoor play in the day helps children fall asleep and sleep better; less sitting, more movement, and daylight in the morning.

lessons.title: التبوّل الليلي: صبرٌ لا عقاب
lessons.focus: Bedwetting is common at this age and out of the child's control: never punish or shame, fewer drinks before bed, the toilet before sleep, a mattress protector, involving the child calmly, praising dry nights; when to see the doctor.

lessons.title: أذكار النوم وحكايةٌ قصيرة
lessons.focus: Ending the day with the bedtime adhkar from a trusted book of adhkar and a short calm story, so sleep is linked to calm and to remembering Allah; no frightening stories.

lessons.title: متى تستشير الطبيب في نومه؟
lessons.focus: Signs that need a doctor: loud snoring, pauses in breathing, persistent difficulty falling or staying asleep, daytime sleepiness or behaviour change, frequent night terrors or sleepwalking, bedwetting returning after months dry or with pain or daytime wetting.
